statement.p: Find the volume of the solid in \mathbf{R}^3 bounded by y=x^2, x=y^2, z=x+y+36, and z=0.

static.solution:
\mathcal{W} is shown in the following figure:
The upper surface is the plane z=x+y+36 and the lower surface is the plane z=0.
The projection of \mathcal{W} onto the xy-plane is the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the curves y={x}^2 and x={y}^2.
We use the formula for the volume as a triple integral to write \mathrm{Volume} (\mathcal{W})=\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 1 \,dV The triple integral is equal to the following iterated integral: \begin{array}{rcl} \mathrm{Volume} (\mathcal{W}) = \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 1 \,dV\amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} \left(\int_0^{x+y+36}1 \,dz\right) \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} z\bigg|_{z=0}^{x+y+36}dA\\ \amp =\amp \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} ( x+y+36 ) \,dA\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \left(\int_{{x}^2}^{\sqrt{x}}( x+y+36 ) \,dy\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 xy+\frac{{y}^2}{2}+36 y\bigg|_{y={x}^2}^{\sqrt{x}}dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1\left(x\sqrt{x}+\frac{x}{2}+36\sqrt{x}-\left({x}^3+\frac{{x}^4}{2} + 36 x^2\right)\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1\left(-\frac{{x}^4}{2}-{x}^3 - 36 {x}^2+{x}^{3/2}+\frac{x}{2}+ 36 {x}^{1/2}\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp -\frac{{x}^5}{10}-\frac{{x}^4}{4}-12 x^3 + \frac{2}{5}{x}^{5/2}+\frac{{x}^2}{4}+24 x^{3/2}\bigg|_0^1\\ \amp =\amp -\frac{1}{10}-\frac{1}{4}-12+\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{4}+24= \frac{246}{20}=12.3 \end{array}
